switches.description: autonomous mode; IDA will not display dialog boxes
switches.notes: Designed to be used together with the -S switch.

switches.description: loading address, a hexadecimal number, in paragraphs (a paragraph is 16 bytes)
batch mode; IDA will generate .IDB and .ASM files automatically
switches.notes: Equivalent to 'ida -c -A -Sanalysis.idc input-file'. Regular plugins are NOT automatically loaded in batch mode, because analysis.idc quits and the kernel has no chance to load them; plugin-driven automation must use 'ida.exe -A -S<script>'. The text interface (idat.exe/idat) is better for batch mode because it uses fewer system resources.

switches.description: disassemble a new file (delete the old database)
a configuration directive which must be processed at the first pass
a configuration directive which must be processed at the second pass

switches.notes: Works for the text version only. Identical to -?, ?, -H and --help; see the -? entry, which carries the whole help family in its aliases.

switches.description: set IDA as just-in-time debugger (0 to disable and 1 to enable)

switches.notes: This switch is not available in the IDA Home edition.

switches.description: do not pack database (not recommended, see Abort command)
load MS Windows exe file resources
execute a script file when the database is opened; the script file extension determines which extlang runs the script
switches.notes: Command line arguments may follow the script name, for example -S"myscript.idc argument1 \"argument 2\" argument3". The passed parameters are stored in the "ARGV" global IDC variable: use "ARGV.count" for the number of arguments; the first argument "ARGV[0]" contains the script name. This switch is not available in the IDA Home edition.

switches.description: interpret the input file as the specified file type; the type is given as a prefix of a file type visible in the 'load file' dialog box
switches.notes: Archive members and nested paths are supported: -TZIP:classes.dex, -T<ftype>[:<member>{:<ftype>:<member>}[:<ftype>]]. IDA does not display the 'load file' dialog in this case.
Used in pair with the Dump database command; this switch affects EXE and COM format files only.

switches.description: debug: enable debug output selected by a hexadecimal bitmask
switches.notes: The hexadecimal bitmask is given after the switch, for example -z40000. See the debug_bits catalog for the meaning of each bit.

switches.description: print the help screen (works for the text version)
switches.notes: The help family. IDA lists -?, ?, -h, -H and --help as separate lines of the help screen, all printing the same screen in the text version (idat.exe/idat) only.

usage_recipes.name: batch
usage_recipes.notes: The text interface (idat.exe/idat) is better for batch mode because it uses fewer system resources.

usage_recipes.name: plugin_automation
usage_recipes.notes: Regular plugins are not automatically loaded in batch mode because the analysis.idc file quits and the kernel has no chance to load them, so plugin-driven automation must use -A -S<script> instead of -B.
